title: From saved inputs and output to a bounded incident assessment
desc: Definition 1.0.0 requires every identifier selected for Northstar with status = active in snapshot S1. The illustrative saved output E12 contains 9,800 rows. Method 2 compares the actual identifier sets and finds 200 required identifiers missing. An Evidence Set supports the Failure Assessment; a Finding, if recorded, derives from that Evidence Set. Neither establishes the cause or recovery.

title: Review, acceptance and two separate histories
desc: A specific proposal goes to a Decision Bundle for review. An authorized Admission Transaction applies the accepted record changes together and saves the updated Project State. One history records what changed; the other records why it was accepted. Both identify the same change event.

texts.text: The saved result of the accepted changes
What changed? The preceding state and resulting state.
Why was it accepted? Decision, authorization and applicable rules.
Both histories refer to the same specific change event.

title: Meaning, required format and the investigation record
desc: The definition explains what Work means. The artifact type sets the required record format. The particular Work record describes the Northstar omission investigation. The arrows explain these roles; they do not create new permitted connections.

texts.text: What does Work mean? A bounded unit of effort.
What must a Work record contain? Declared fields and constraints.

title: The Northstar agent session and its durable project records
desc: Project State retains the investigation observation, candidate revision 8, decisions and evidence. Context View 3 and an Ontology View select exact information for session 12. The temporary session binds one agent instance, its assignment, delegation, actions and working memory. View 3 later expires, requiring a checked replacement and current permission before continuing.

title: From the reported problem to the agent’s investigation job
desc: Intent states the desired change. Intent Resolution selects a response and satisfaction test. The value column identifies the Product, Product Capability, version-specific realization binding and Implementation. The work column identifies the repair Project, Goal, investigation Work and Agent Assignment. The Incident keeps its response and closure responsibilities.

texts.text: Let customers obtain their complete eligible data.
Choose a response and how to assess success.

title: Experience, later lesson use and assessment
desc: Read three stages in order: record the incident investigation through an Operational Observation, propose advice for future work where data can change between batches, then record its use or deliberate non-use and assess the predicted benefit. That advice does not establish the cause or remedy of the fixed-snapshot Northstar incident. The SVG label Work observation refers to the Operational Observation record kind.

texts.text: Evidence: recorded failed run and row comparison. Applies when data can change between batch requests. Excludes fixed-data exports with a different integrity contract. Predicted benefit: detect missing rows before delivery. Contradicted if a checked export still delivers missing rows.
Name the lesson version. Record use or deliberate non-use.
Compare the prediction with the observed result and evidence.
Changing rules or code requires its own authorization.

title: How local shortcuts accumulate design debt
desc: A new request leads to a convenient patch, duplicated or entangled responsibilities, harder subsequent changes and pressure for another local workaround.

title: The four families of active backend roles
desc: Structural roles are Entity, Value Object and Enum. Behavioral roles are Operation, Query, Calculation, Rule, Policy and Workflow. Connective roles are Interface, Event and Mapping. The lifecycle role is State Machine.

title: From domain meaning to compiled artifacts and recorded observations
desc: Domain definitions inform a project model. Validation checks its declarations under selected architecture constraints. The compiler uses selected realizations to construct artifacts. Observations of exact targets and records of performed work are preserved in project state.

title: The capacity decision has two normal outcomes and no mutation
desc: The supplied snapshot is evaluated by Within capacity. Requested units strictly below available units produce Accept. Equality or a larger request produces Reject. Both branches return without changing state.

title: Typed references connect the pure capacity classifier to its inputs, Rule and result
desc: Classify capacity is a Calculation. Its input type refers to Capacity snapshot, its condition calls Within capacity through a typed Rule reference, and its result type refers to Capacity decision. All three arrows represent typed references, not authored graph relationship kinds.

title: Four separate questions about the capacity implementation
desc: Model validation checks declarations and connections. Artifact verification checks code against its selection. Behavioral evaluation checks execution against expected outcomes. Completion review checks which required actions have evidence of performance.

title: Revising a condition and adding reservation require different design changes
desc: Allowing equality revises the acceptance definition, Rule and expected outcomes. Reserving capacity adds a state-changing responsibility with ownership, consistency and failure contracts. Each successor needs design review and its own construction and evaluation evidence.

title: Project state carries design knowledge between ephemeral agent sessions
desc: A session records its work in durable project state. Context views select task-relevant information, and ontology views expose recorded concepts and relationships. A later ephemeral session uses those views while maintaining only its own short-term memory.

title: Authority, provenance and lifecycle are three lenses on the same subject
desc: A particular definition, model, artifact or work record can be examined for its governing meaning and permissions, its origin and evidence, and its current state and required transitions. These are independent governance questions.
